4.label: Completion and capability
4.text: Implementation is incomplete until the gains can be sustained. Distinguish project completion from sustained capability, and protect results through ownership, resourcing, monitoring and corrective action, because they regress when maintenance weakens.

4.label: Cumulative decline
4.text: Organisations rarely fail through a single catastrophic decision. Decline is cumulative: neglected principles, ignored warnings and normalised unhealthy behaviour gradually weaken the systems designed to sustain success.

5.label: Responsiveness to signal
5.text: Effective organisations build responsiveness to external signals into their operating culture. Organisations that follow internal plans regardless of external signals miss the moments when conditions move differently from the plan.

5.label: The wrong posture for the season
5.text: Organisations most often drift into trouble by occupying a posture suited to a different time. Diagnose what season the work is actually in and whether your position matches it.

6.label: Momentum Illusion
6.text: Organisations anchor confidence in established structures (market positions, legacy products, long-standing advantages) that are quietly on a clock. Identify which apparent permanences are temporary, and build security on what will outlast them.

6.label: At the peak
6.text: When a business is at its peak, the disciplines that produced the peak are most at risk of being quietly abandoned. Review the practices that built the current position and name any that have been set aside.

6.label: Execution Regression
6.text: After key milestones, strategic focus can fragment as attention shifts from enterprise outcomes to individual or team recognition. Priorities lose sharpness and execution becomes less coordinated.

7.label: K · Keep
7.text: Before the environment applies its pressure, decide what must be preserved for the organisation to remain itself, and which commitments are open to negotiation.

7.label: S · Stop
7.text: Leaders accumulate programmes built to reproduce past breakthroughs. Identify one that exists mainly because something like it succeeded before, check whether it still produces the original effect, and schedule its sunset if the case for keeping it is mostly nostalgia.

7.label: S · Start
7.text: The end of one source of revenue is the prompt to commit to the next before necessity forces a scramble. Build the transition while the old stream still trickles.

9.label: Cosmetic continuity
9.text: Organisations often respond to decline by reproducing the appearance of what once worked without restoring the capability, discipline or substance that made it valuable. Symbols, reports and routines remain intact while quality deteriorates. Use this with Execution Regression and Success Inertia.

9.label: Speed and soundness
9.text: Organisations that draw their confidence from operating speed are one disruption away from a crisis they cannot outrun. Speed is an advantage; soundness is a requirement.

10.label: Success Inertia
10.text: The most dangerous period for an organisation is a prolonged season of success, because that is when preparation for resilience is deprioritised.

10.label: After a near-miss
10.text: When a crisis eases, the common response is relief with no reform. After every close call, ask: what condition produced this, and have we changed it?

13.label: Inherited assumptions
13.text: Leaders become blockers of growth when they treat inherited assumptions as permanent truth. Recognise when evidence or context is challenging an old boundary. Use this with Step 3 of the navigation chain.

13.label: V · Is the edge still holding?
13.text: Strong cash positions, market share, brands or technology can come to be treated as guarantees of future relevance. Ask: what are we assuming these assets will continue to do for us?

14.label: Fixed and adaptable
14.text: Sound strategy identifies what must remain fixed (purpose, values and direction) while allowing responses to circumstances to adapt. Uncertainty should not automatically produce frantic activity.

16.label: Systems behind decisions
16.text: The wisest strategic insight is only as durable as the system built to sustain it. Find one good decision with no system behind it to hold the outcome, and build the system.

16.label: After the pressure eases
16.text: A culture’s true posture shows in what people do once the threat has lifted. Name one disciplined practice from the last hard season and decide whether it is still honoured.

19.label: First principles under pressure
19.text: Pressure tempts leaders to confuse urgent relief with sound direction. Difficult conditions should drive a return to first principles.

19.label: Drift by accommodation
19.text: A venture can drift, one reasonable accommodation at a time, into a commitment that runs against its own purpose. Trace the largest current commitment back through the decisions that led to it and confirm the destination still matches the intent.

20.label: Outliving the architects
20.text: Sustainable strategies are designed to outlive their architects. Structure should support purpose, and continuity should be planned before transition becomes necessary.
